provenance.instrument: City of Lancaster Zoning, Chapter 300 (Ord. No. 6-2013, adopted 7-23-2013), with 300 Attachment 2 Table of Permitted Uses and 300 Attachment 3 Table of Height, Area and Bulk Regulations
provenance.status_detail: The zoning chapter has no accessory dwelling unit or similar term. Searched definitions (Art XVII), the Table of Permitted Uses, accessory uses (300-16), accessory structures (300-27), multiple principal buildings (300-28), conversions (300-31) and parking (300-41, 300-44). eCode360 New Laws for Ch 300: Ord. No. 07-2026 (7-14-2026, data centers). Not ADU related.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 header: Includes legislation through 12-16-2025. Use table PDF marked Supp 39, Dec 2023. Bulk table PDF marked Supp 38, Feb 2023.
checks: No ADU, accessory apartment, in-law or similar term in the zoning chapter

An accessory unit is a use not provided for. The Zoning Officer refers it to the Zoning Hearing Board as a special exception (300-17). The applicant shows it is similar to and compatible with permitted uses
Accessory uses may not exceed 25% of the principal use floor area (300-16). A dwelling unit as an accessory use is not listed
Each dwelling unit holds one family or one nonfamily unit. Family: relatives plus at most one unrelated person, or two unrelated persons (Art XVII)
Minimum habitable floor area: efficiency 400, one bedroom 550, two bedrooms 700 sq ft (300-30)

Other ways to add a unit are listed in approval.alternatives: a second principal dwelling (300-28A) and a two-family conversion (R3, R4, RO, MU, C1, C2). Ask the Bureau of Planning whether lot area must cover two dwellings
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Bureau of Planning, Department of Community Planning and Economic Development (page in source_urls). Pending changes: none found that affect ADUs. Census GEOID is the 2020 county subdivision code from TIGERweb.

status.note: No accessory dwelling term or use in the zoning chapter.

term.note: No term. Searched for: accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, ADU, in-law, granny, ECHO, elder cottage, carriage house, secondary dwelling, second dwelling. Nearest text: 'a second residential unit is proposed in a separate building as per § 300-28A' (300-44E).

path.note: A use neither specifically permitted nor prohibited goes to the Zoning Hearing Board as a special exception. It may be permitted if similar to and compatible with permitted uses in the district.

fallback_path.note: If the Board finds the unit not similar to permitted uses, a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board is left.

unlisted_use_path.note: 'a use is neither specifically permitted nor prohibited' goes to the Zoning Hearing Board 'to hear and decide such request as a special exception'.

value.name: Second dwelling in a separate building (more than one principal residential building on a lot)
value.conditions: Yard and other requirements met for the entire lot. Parking for the added unit may be reduced by special exception (300-44E). Whether lot area must cover both dwellings is not stated.

value.name: Conversion of an existing building of at least 2,000 gross sq ft to a two-family dwelling
value.conditions: Not in R1 or R2. If the building is not enlarged, lot area, yards, width, depth, height and coverage may be waived when coverage does not increase and parking is provided (300 Attachment 3 note (d)).

zoning_districts.note: No ADU use in any district. Any district may hear it as a use not provided for (300-17). Two-family conversion by special exception in R3, R4, RO, MU, C1, C2.

min_lot_sqft.note: No ADU rule. District lot area per dwelling applies to a second principal dwelling. How it is counted is not stated.

types_allowed.note: No ADU forms. The form would be set by the Zoning Hearing Board under 300-17. A separate building can be a second principal dwelling under 300-28A. A unit inside the house can be a two-family conversion.

max_sqft.note: No ADU cap. Accessory uses may not exceed 25% of the gross floor area of the principal use.

max_share_of_house.note: No ADU share. The 25% accessory use cap applies to accessory uses in general.

min_sqft.note: Efficiency unit: 400 square feet. One bedroom 550. Two bedrooms 700.

max_height_ft.note: No separate accessory structure height cap found. District height applies.

setback_front_ft.note: No accessory structure of any kind shall be erected or placed in any required front, secondary front, or side yard.

setback_side_ft.note: Accessory structures: three-foot setback from side or rear lot line, or less with a recorded easement. A dwelling in a separate building is a principal building and meets district yards. See districts.

setback_rear_ft.note: Accessory structures 3 ft. A separate dwelling building meets principal yards. See districts.

max_building_coverage.note: Set by district and use. See districts.

max_impervious.note: Total coverage set by district and use. See districts notes.

owner_occupancy.note: No ADU rule, so no owner occupancy rule.

spaces_required.note: One or more dwelling and/or efficiency units: 1 per dwelling and/or efficiency unit. 300-44E allows a special exception to reduce it for a second unit in a separate building.

min_lot_sqft.note: Lot area for one single-family detached dwelling.

setback_side_ft.note: Principal side yard. Accessory structures: 3 ft (300-27D).

setback_rear_ft.note: Principal rear yard. Accessory structures may sit in it, 3 ft from lines (300-27D).

min_lot_sqft.note: Lot area for one single-family detached dwelling.

setback_front_ft.note: Front yard. Note (b) build-to rules apply in R2 and R3.

setback_rear_ft.note: Principal rear yard. Accessory structures may sit in it, 3 ft from lines (300-27D).
